cost_basis: DERIVED from R1's OWN MEASURED per-level actuals for the same configuration -- L1 0.94 / L2 5.11 / L3 21.89 core-min (total 27.94), read from each level's final ExecutionTime and verified by the supervisor against the run artifacts. Scaled x3 for the R2 endTime of 60000 (R1 ran 20000), giving 83.82, plus a stated 10% instrumentation margin for the refining sampler (nPoints 321/641/1281 vs R1's flat 400) = 92.20; FILED 92, a round-down (-0.2%). This deliberately avoids R1's 2.33x miss, whose cause was diagnosed at charter section 27.3: R1 priced a run under residualControl and then removed residualControl in the same document, so its estimate described a different workload than the one that ran. Here the basis is the measured actual OF THE CONFIGURATION BEING RE-RUN and the single workload change (endTime x3) is applied explicitly. Section 27's opposite trap -- a cap at ~3x an UNDER-filed estimate strangling its own run after the compute is spent -- is avoided from the other side: the 276 cap sits 9.9x above R1's whole-triple measured actual, and per-level caps 9.3/50.6/216.7 mean an L1 or L2 overrun cannot consume L3's budget. Serial, RANKS=1, matching R1 exactly so the actuals transfer. ~$0.079 DERIVED at $0.0513/core-h c7a.4xlarge, owner-stated -- NOT measured; the box cannot read its own billing (COMPUTE_BUDGET_CHARTER section 5).
